Operating within Rumdel Construction’s civil delivery teams, the role ensures works are completed safely, on program, within budget and in accordance with contract specifications, Australian Standards and relevant Transport for NSW (TfNSW) and local government requirements. Technical & Quality Management   - Supervise asphalt milling to specified depth, profile and cross-fall, ensuring surface preparation meets design requirements.   - Oversee in-situ stabilisation works, including binder spread rates, mixing depth, moisture conditioning and compaction.   - Manage spray sealing operations, including binder and aggregate application rates, temperatures and sequencing.   - Control asphalt paving and compaction to achieve specified thickness, density, joint quality and ride characteristics.   - Verify conformance against Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), TfNSW/MRTS specifications and approved hold and witness points.   Safety, Environment & Compliance   - Implement and enforce WHS requirements, Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS) and safe systems of work on all activities.   - Manage worksite traffic in accordance with approved Traffic Guidance Schemes and Traffic Management Plans.  - Conduct pre-start meetings, toolbox talks, hazard identification and risk assessments.  - Ensure environmental controls for dust, noise, spillage and water management are maintained.   Plant, Resources & Productivity   - Direct the operation and allocation of milling machines, stabilisers, pavers, rollers, sprayers and support plant.  - Monitor production rates, material usage and wastage to optimise cost and program outcomes.  - Coordinate deliveries of asphalt, aggregates and binders, and liaise with suppliers and the asphalt plant.   Communication, Reporting & Stakeholder Relations   - Maintain accurate site records, daily diaries, quality records and as-built information.  - Liaise with the Project Manager, clients, superintendents, council representatives and the community.  - Provide on-the-job direction, training and mentoring to operators, labourers and apprentices.  - Report progress, productivity, incidents and non-conformances to project management.   Qualification & experience   Skills & Competencies   - Strong practical knowledge of road rehabilitation and pavement construction methods (milling, in-situ stabilisation, spray seal and asphalt paving).  - Ability to interpret civil engineering drawings, pavement designs and technical specifications, including TfNSW and MRTS standards.  - Sound understanding of WHS legislation, traffic management and environmental compliance in civil works.  - Proven ability to plan, coordinate and supervise labour, plant and subcontractors to program.  - Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving and decision-making skills.  - Commercial awareness of production rates, materials control and cost management.   Qualifications & Accreditation   - Relevant qualification in Civil Construction or Construction Management, or equivalent demonstrated experience (minimum five years) in civil road construction supervision.  - Demonstrated experience supervising asphalt, in-situ stabilisation and sprayed sealing works.  - General Construction Induction Card (White Card).  - Traffic management accreditation (for example, Prepare a Work Zone Traffic Management Plan) desirable.  - Current driver licence; relevant plant and high-risk work licences desirable. As a community midwife in the heart of the thriving rural town of Bourke you'll be building relationships, providing information and giving support to the women of the Bourke district and their babies. 

As well as being actively involved in giving antenatal advice and helping parent prepare for birth, you will attend to postnatal needs for the first 10 days post-birth, mostly in the homes of the new mothers. You will help new mothers look after themselves and their baby including parenting, infant feeding, settling, sleep and other related topics as guided by the needs, expectations and aspirations of the women in your care.

Bourke is a beautiful historic town set on the banks of the Darling River -one of Australia's most important rivers. The Bourke Shire (local government area) has an area of approximately 43,000 square kilometres and is home to around 3000 people, with the Shire's prosperity built around the pastoral, irrigation, tourism and service industries which are strongly supported by a wide range of attractions and activities.
